# Optimization and Training

Also called: 3D Gaussian Splatting Training, 3DGS Optimization

## Overview
Optimization and Training refers to the iterative procedure that adjusts the parameters of a collection of 3D Gaussian primitives to minimize the perceptual and geometric distortion between rendered views and ground-truth images [S1, S2]. It solves the problem of learning a scene representation by using differentiable rendering to backpropagate pixel errors through alpha compositing and projection to update Gaussian geometry, color, and opacity [S2]. It is distinguished from its siblings by its specific reliance on adaptive densification driven by gradient magnitudes to dynamically modulate the number of Gaussians, ensuring a trade-off between reconstruction quality and representation budget [S1].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family optimize a set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. Each primitive $i$ is defined by:
*   Position $\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$
*   Rotation $q_i \in \mathbb{R}^4$ (unit quaternion)
*   Scale $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$
*   Opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$
*   Appearance parameters (e.g., spherical harmonic coefficients $h_i$) [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]

The optimization minimizes a loss function $\mathcal{L}$ between rendered images and ground truth views, typically using the Adam optimizer [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. The rendering process involves projecting 3D Gaussians to 2D screen space, sorting by depth, and alpha blending [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].

## Subtopics

### [RadSplat](8059-radsplat.md)
RadSplat is a method for initializing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scenes by leveraging a pre-trained Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) to generate a dense, topologically correct point cloud, which is then converted into Gaussians. It solves the problem of poor initialization quality and topological artifacts inherent in raw Structure-from-Motion (SfM) point clouds, enabling high-quality rendering with unprecedented speed. Unlike feed-forward methods like MVSplat that regress parameters directly, RadSplat uses a hybrid approach that bypasses the per-scene gradient descent loop for initialization.

### [Training Optimization and Initialization](13464-training-optimization-and-initialization.md)
This family covers the initialization strategies and iterative optimization procedures required to reconstruct 3D scenes from 2D images using 3D Gaussian Splatting [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It solves the problem of converting sparse or dense image collections into a set of differentiable volumetric primitives that can be rendered in real time [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It differs from implicit neural field methods by optimizing explicit, static or dynamic ellipsoids via differentiable rasterization, achieving faster convergence and rendering speeds [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].

### [3D Gaussian Splatting Optimization](15143-3d-gaussian-splatting-optimization.md)
3D Gaussian Splatting Optimization is the training procedure that adjusts the parameters of a collection of 3D Gaussian primitives to minimize the perceptual and geometric distortion between rendered views and ground-truth images. It solves the problem of learning scene representation by using differentiable rendering to backpropagate pixel errors through alpha compositing and projection to update Gaussian geometry, color, and opacity. It is distinguished from its siblings by its specific reliance on adaptive densification driven by gradient magnitudes to dynamically modulate the number of Gaussians, ensuring a trade-off between reconstruction quality and representation budget.

### [Optimization and Regularization](17383-optimization-and-regularization.md)

### 3D Gaussian Splatting with Frequency-Domain Regularization
- [S1] Applies frequency-domain regularization to the rendered 2D image to encourage high-frequency detail recovery.

### GSGEN Geometry Optimization
#### definition
- [S2] Optimization process to shape reasonable 3D geometry by integrating a 3D SDS loss with a pre-trained point cloud diffusion model (Point-E) to mitigate the Janus problem.
#### step
- [S2] Optimize Gaussian positions using Point-E guidance via 3D SDS loss, avoiding direct alignment to avoid registration/scaling/degeneration challenges.
#### formula
- [S2] \nabla_\theta L_{geometry} = E_{\epsilon_I, t} w_I(t)(\epsilon_\phi(x_t; y, t) - \epsilon_I) \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta} + \lambda_{3D} \cdot E_{\epsilon_P, t} [w_P(t)(\epsilon_\psi(p_t; y, t) - \epsilon_P)] \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta}, where p_t is noisy Gaussian positions, x_t is rendered image, w* is weighting function, \epsilon* is Gaussian noise.
#### parameter
- [S2] \lambda_{3D} = 0.01, loss weight for 3D prior in geometry optimization stage.

## Background
The optimization of 3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced alongside the original 3DGS method [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It builds on [3D Gaussian Splatting](2812-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) by providing the differentiable training loop necessary to learn scene parameters from 2D observations. The approach has been extended to address specific challenges such as initialization quality [8059-radsplat.md], frequency detail recovery [S1], and geometry consistency in text-to-3D generation [S2].
